new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level, tentative: in the Tirio (Lower Fly) Family languages -- Wurm's Tirio, Aturu (= Makayam of Aduru), Lewada-Dewara and Mutum, surveyed jointly from his own field materials -- stress 'appears to be phonemic' (i.e. contrastive, position not predictable), with a 'complex rhythm system'; vowel length also phonemic; no tone. No positional rule, no examples, and no language-by-language breakdown are given.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing beyond the undefined 'complex rhythm system' / 'rhythm principles' (Wurm 1971:144, 161; 1975:331).
new_statements.exceptions: None; the whole statement is hedged ('appears to be', 'results of a superficial phonological study are still tentative').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology implied (phoneme inventory context); statement is generic over the four Tirio-Family lects, not specific to Makayam; based on Wurm's and UFM missionaries' unpublished field materials (p.142).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is generic over Wurm's 'Tirio Family' (Tirio, Aturu, Lewada-Dewara, Mutum). Of these, 'Aturu' (Adulu/Aduru village, Sumogi Island) and the Lewada/Balamula part of 'Lewada-Dewara' correspond to today's Makayam (maka1315); per Usher (NewGuineaWorld, following Jore & Alemán 2002) Wurm's/Riley's 'Tirio' village lect = Baramu (bara1380), Dewala = Were, Mutum/Paswam = Bitur (bitu1242). Glottolog lists 'Tirio' as an alt name of maka1315 only because ISO aup was formerly labelled Tirio. No source describes Makayam (or its Giribam dialect) individually.
